title: Oratio Solennis & Quatuor Temporum. De Superstitiosa Pontificiorum Ceremonia ... Festum Corporis Christi

structure_note: 22 pages: 22 with OCR, 21 translated. The sampled pages run in order. Publication date is 'Unknown'.

title: Boethius De consolatione philosophiae

structure_note: 102 pages, 96 with OCR, 92 translated. The pencil foliation (10 on image 25, 25 on image 55) is consistent with rectos and versos imaged separately; nothing out of order.

shelf_note: A 1651 Wittenberg feudal-law disputation (Suevus praeses); fits the europeanlibraries collection.
structure_note: 20 pages, all with OCR and all translated. Section numbers on the sampled pages run in order (II, V, IX).

ocr_errors.problem: the abbreviation 'extraord.' (a citation) is expanded into an adjective governing 'women and men'; the English follows ('Chapter 100, extraordinary, to women and men')

tr_errors.source: ut juvet Dominum adversus omnes, excepto Imperatore vel Rege ... & antiquiore Domino ... patriâ quoque & se ipso
tr_errors.english: that he may aid the Lord against all, except the Emperor or King ... and the older Lord. ... Also against the fatherland and himself.
tr_errors.problem: sense reversed: the fatherland and the vassal himself are further EXCEPTIONS (ablative with excepto); the English says the vassal must aid the lord against his own country

tr_errors.source: Illud affirmantes, hoc negantes: uni tantùm ... jurandum esse
tr_errors.english: Affirming it, denying this: that it must be sworn in the name of all by one only
tr_errors.problem: the two camps (some affirm, others deny that one may swear for all) are collapsed

book_verdict: Accurate transcription of a dense legal disputation and a generally careful translation, but one legal point is reversed: on p.15 the vassal is made to aid his lord 'against the fatherland and himself' where the text exempts them. Abbreviation expansion is inconsistent between pages.
